content: Amoxicillin is indicated for the treatment of infections in the ear, nose, and throat caused by susceptible strains of Streptococcus species (including alphaand beta-hemolytic strains), Streptococcus pneumoniae, or Haemophilus influenzae. Amoxicillin is indicated for the treatment of infections of the genitourinary tract caused by susceptible strains of Escherichia coli, Proteus mirabilis, or Enterococcus faecalis. Amoxicillin is indicated for the treatment of infections of the skin and skin structures caused by susceptible strains of Streptococcus species or Escherichia coli. Amoxicillin is indicated for the treatment of infections of the lower respiratory tract caused by susceptible strains of Streptococcus species (including alphaand beta-hemolytic strains), Streptococcus pneumoniae, or Haemophilus influenzae. Amoxicillin is indicated for the treatment of acute, uncomplicated gonorrhea (anogenital and urethral infections) caused by Neisseria gonorrhoeae in both males and females. Amoxicillin, in combination with clarithromycin and lansoprazole as part of triple therapy, is indicated for the treatment of patients with Helicobacter pylori infection and duodenal ulcer disease (active or with a one-year history of a duodenal ulcer) to eradicate H. pylori. The eradication of H. pylori has been shown to reduce the risk of duodenal ulcer recurrence. Amoxicillin, in combination with lansoprazole delayed-release capsules as part of dual therapy, is indicated for the treatment of patients with Helicobacter pylori infection and duodenal ulcer disease (active or with a one-year history of a duodenal ulcer) who are either allergic or intolerant to clarithromycin or in whom resistance to clarithromycin is known or suspected. The eradication of H. pylori has been shown to reduce the risk of duodenal ulcer recurrence. To minimize the development of drug-resistant bacteria and maintain the effectiveness of amoxicillin and other antibacterial drugs, amoxicillin should only be used to treat or prevent infections that are proven or strongly suspected to be caused by susceptible bacteria. When culture and susceptibility data are available, they should be considered in selecting or modifying antibacterial therapy. In the absence of such data, local epidemiology and susceptibility patterns may contribute to the empiric selection of therapy. Indicated surgical procedures should also be performed. Amoxicillin is specifically indicated for the treatment of infections caused by susceptible (only beta-lactamase–negative) strains of the designated microorganisms.
